operational-example.copy: Use Floating Action Button for one primary contextual action that belongs to the current surface.

scenario.title: Floating Action Button
scenario.meta: Expose one high-prominence contextual action above a surface with FAB-specific treatment variants.
rationale: Use Floating Action Button for one contextual action that belongs to the current surface.
FAB variants describe treatment: primary, extended, or mini. Button/IconButton own action hierarchy variants.
Use extended labels when ambiguity is risky and avoid covering critical content on small screens.

items.rule: Circular or extended action target above the current surface.
Clarifies extended actions without replacing aria-label.
Separates the action from underlying content.
Shows keyboard focus, loading, pressed, and disabled states.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, loading, pressed, focus, hover, default
items: Provide a visible accessible label for the control.
Expose current state and relationship through ARIA where applicable.
Support keyboard focus and expected dismissal or selection keys.
Do not rely on color alone for selected, warning, loading, or disabled state.
Escalate to a pattern when orchestration exceeds one component.

variants.copy: Floating Action Button variants describe FAB treatment; danger and warning are intents.

states.copy: Floating Action Button states communicate focus, pressed, loading, and disabled for a single command.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines FAB treatment; state defines readiness; intent defines semantic risk.

full-width.copy: Floating Action Button does not fill containers; extended mode may grow to fit a concise label while preserving a single action.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use extended labels when ambiguity is risky, compact density only in dense contexts, and avoid covering critical content on small screens.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport rules place the action where it is reachable and non-obstructive; they do not add secondary actions.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use touch-safe targets and avoid covering critical content.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the component close to the surface it controls.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density only when labels and focus remain visible.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify icon, label, variant, state, and whether the action remains single-purpose.

api-foundations.copy: Floating Action Button API exposes label, icon, variant, state, position, and loading while Design System owns elevation, focus, and target size.

props.name: variant
props.notes: FAB treatment: primary, extended, or mini. Action hierarchy belongs to Button/IconButton.

props.name: intent
props.notes: Action intent aligned with Button: default, danger, warning.

props.name: loading
props.notes: Shows busy state for the invoked action.

props.name: extended
props.notes: Shows the label beside the icon without changing action hierarchy.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for one contextual primary action.
Keep the action close to the surface it affects.
Use extended mode when the icon is ambiguous.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not put multiple actions inside FAB.
Do not cover critical content or controls.
Do not use FAB for global navigation.

groups.title: Review
items: Check target size and safe area.
Check overlap with maps, sheets, and bottom navigation.

rejectIf: FAB contains more than one command.
The icon has no accessible label.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Floating Action Button as one contextual high-prominence action. Agents may place it when the primary action is obvious, while humans confirm placement, label, overlap, and whether multiple actions require a pattern.
canDecide: Use FAB for create, add movement, center map, scan receipt, or start route when it is the sole primary action.
Use extended FAB when the label prevents ambiguity.
Use loading only for the invoked action.
mustAsk: The surface has bottom navigation, sheets, or map controls that may be covered.
The action has financial, safety, or irreversible consequences.
rejectIf: FAB contains more than one command.
The icon has no accessible label.
miel.handoff: I am using Floating Action Button for one contextual action. Please confirm label, icon, placement, safe-area overlap, loading behavior, and whether this should be a Quick Action pattern.
